title: Speculative runtime acceptance & rollback matrix
summary: Draft design and operational checklist for integrating speculative decoding into the runtime, including kernel selection heuristics, scheduler changes, KV cache behavior, acceptance criteria, rollback triggers, and the metrics to observably validate correctness and performance.
background: We want to deploy speculative decoding to reduce tail latency for large autoregressive requests while preserving cost constraints and model quality. Speculative decoding introduces multi-path execution, temporary duplication of work (speculative prefixes), and a dependency on fast kernel selection and cache coherence. This doc captures a pragmatic integration approach and an operational matrix for rollout and rollback.
goals: 1) Reduce p95 token latency for long-context generator flows by >=20% on target workloads. 2) Maintain token cost delta <= +8% at steady state. 3) No detectable quality regression on critical eval sets (<=1% delta in quality score). 4) Provide clear rollback triggers and automated safeguards.
non_goals: 1) Full redesign of kernel ABI. 2) Handling of all research variants of speculative algorithms (this is pragmatic production variant only).
proposed_changes: Introduce a speculative execution path in the request pipeline that can spawn a cheap fast-model speculative head alongside the main model; add a scheduler priority class for speculative work; extend KV cache semantics to support ephemeral speculative keys and a small pinned prefix cache for hot prompts; add kernel probing to select optimal attention/MatMul kernels for speculative fragments based on sequence length and quantization format.
kernel_strategy: Rule-based selection: 1) Probe at model load for supported kernels by sequence-length buckets (<=64, 65-512, >512) and quantization mode (fp16/int8/q4). 2) Maintain small per-model kernel preference table that maps (sequence_bucket, layer_type) -> kernel_id. 3) At runtime, for speculative fragments we prefer lowest-latency kernels with acceptable accuracy profiles; fallback to stable kernel for finalization. 4) Periodic background rebenchmarking during low load to refresh preferences.
scheduler_changes: 1) Add 'speculative' priority queue that is preemptible and best-effort. 2) Speculative tasks get lower memory reservation; if main request completes earlier, speculative result is discarded. 3) Implement speculative concurrency limit per GPU (default 2 per-GPU) to bound resource amplification. 4) Batching: allow speculative fragments to join small fast batches (batch cap 8) while main model uses standard batching.
kv_cache_design: 1) Two-tier KV cache per model: pinned-prefix cache (small, ~8MB per-shard) for common prompts and ephemeral speculative cache for in-flight speculative fragments. 2) Ephemeral cache entries have TTL tied to request lifetime and do not persist across requests. 3) Eviction: LRU for pinned-prefix; ephemeral entries are deallocated immediately after speculative path completes or is cancelled. 4) Consistency: when a speculative fragment produces KV state that is later used by main model, we support a fast copy path into persistent KV region only after verification step. 5) Metrics expose kv_pinned_hit_rate and kv_ephemeral_hit_rate.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: 1) Speculative path produces stable outputs that can be validated by merge logic in 99.9% of test requests in unit harness. 2) No memory leaks after 48h soak on canary hosts. Performance: 1) p95 token latency improves >=20% on synthetic long-tail workload with 90th percentile seq length >256. 2) End-to-end token cost increase <=8% compared to baseline. Quality: 1) Eval suite (regression-prompts-v2) shows <=1% drop in quality score. Observability: 1) All speculative metrics emitted (speculative_attempts, speculative_success_rate, speculative_waste_ratio, kv_pinned_hit_rate, kv_ephemeral_hit_rate). Security/compliance: 1) KV ephemeral data is not written to persistent logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary on dev cluster with synthetic traffic, 2 nodes, 24-48h. Phase 1: Canary real traffic 1% of requests in us-west for 24h. Phase 2: Expand to 5% across two regions for 72h. Phase 3: 25% over 7 days with automated checks. Phase 4: full 100% if all checks green. Each phase has automatic rollback conditions and manual gates for owner approval.
rollback_triggers: Immediate rollback triggers: 1) p95 latency regression >5% sustained for 15m vs baseline. 2) Increase in request error rate >0.5 percentage points. 3) Quality regression on monitored eval set >1.5% in production compare. 4) Speculative_waste_ratio >60% for >10m and cost delta >12%. 5) Memory pressure leading to OOM events. Soft rollback/slowdown: throttle speculative concurrency when speculative_error_rate >1% or kv_ephemeral_mem > configured threshold.
monitoring_metrics: List: p50_token_latency, p95_token_latency, tokens_per_second, model_fallback_rate, speculative_attempts, speculative_success_rate, speculative_waste_ratio, kv_pinned_hit_rate, kv_ephemeral_hit_rate, rollout_request_fraction, token_cost_delta_percent, generation_error_rate, quality_regression_score, kernel_selection_mismatch_rate.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for kernel mapping table and fallback semantics. 2) Integration tests: golden-run harness that replays recorded long-tail requests with deterministic RNG and compares outputs. 3) Chaos tests: kill speculative worker mid-request to validate recovery. 4) Load soak: 48h at 2x expected speculative concurrency. 5) A/B evaluation with live traffic and blind quality scoring on red-team prompts.
operational_playbook: 1) Alerting: page on p95 regression, speculative_error_rate >1%, kv_memory_pressure. 2) Quick diagnostic runbook: check speculative_attempts, waste_ratio, last kernel probe logs, kv eviction counts, recent rollouts. 3) Remediation steps: reduce speculative_fraction to 0.1, decrease per-GPU speculative limit, or disable speculative path via feature flag. 4) Post-incident: capture trace, kernel probe snapshot, and run mini-eval on affected traffic.
risks_and_mitigations: Risks: increased cost due to wasted speculative work, cache thrash, quality regressions, kernel incompatibilities on older GPUs. Mitigations: conservative defaults, ephemeral cache isolation, per-GPU speculative caps, automated quality checks, selective kernel blacklisting via config.
estimated_timeline: Discovery + proto: 3 weeks. Kernel probe and KV changes: 2 weeks. Scheduler + batching updates: 2 weeks. Internal canary + soak: 2 weeks. External canary ramp: 4 weeks. Total nominal: 13 weeks.

next_steps: 1) Approve acceptance thresholds and rollback triggers. 2) Create infra PR for kernel probing and small pinned-prefix cache. 3) Implement scheduler priority queue and speculative concurrency limits. 4) Wire metrics and dashboards before canary. 5) Schedule canary window and coordinate with SRE.
notes_to_reviewers: Focus review on acceptance thresholds and rollback triggers; we biased conservatively on cost and latency tradeoffs. If you have strong use-cases where pinned-prefix sizes should be larger, flag now — changing after rollout is high risk.
